what_it_does.name: audit-website
what_it_does.summary: Instructions for auditing a website with the squirrel CLI and fixing the findings in the site's code. The agent runs squirrel audit against a URL with the LLM report format, presents the score, grade and top issues, maps each issue to the template, component or content file behind it, applies the fixes the user approves in batches and re-audits until a score target is met. A reference file describes the LLM report and diff format. Use it to discover and assess website or webapp issues and drive them to fixed.
tasks: audit a website against 300+ rules with the squirrel CLI
map audit issues to the templates, components or content files behind them
fix approved issues in batches and re-audit until the score target is met
compare audits against a baseline to catch regressions
tailor audits by disabling rules that do not apply to the site
start the fix loop from a squirrelscan channel event

risks.risk: Instructions hidden in a crawled page or a channel event reach the agent through the audit report, while the agent can edit the project's source code.
risks.severity: MEDIUM by C1, SAFE overall by C2
risks.mitigation: in the instructions, event text is treated as data and the user confirms before any change, no technical boundary

risks.risk: Repeated re-audits in the fix loop spend squirrelscan credits when signed in, 50 plus 2 per audited page on every pass.
risks.mitigation: signed out or with --offline it costs nothing, and a quick first pass caps pages at 25

risks.risk: Web Bot Auth header values passed with -H on the command line can stay in shell history or logs.
risks.mitigation: header values are redacted in squirrel output, shell history not addressed

limitations: A skipped check is not clean and is not reported as fixed.
Exit codes 3, 4 and 5 mean nothing was audited and there is no score.
Requests listed under refused-fetches are unknown, not missing.
A local dev server does not show true rendering, performance and redirect behaviour.
The quick pass samples only part of the site, so sign-off needs a --level full crawl.
A published report is a capped summary that samples affected pages, so fixes come from the local report.
Broken links and other judgment calls need a human decision.

known_problems.problem: the site blocks unknown crawlers, such as Shopify or Cloudflare
known_problems.workaround: pass Web Bot Auth headers with repeated -H flags

known_problems.problem: the start URL redirected to another site
known_problems.workaround: relay the destination and re-run with --follow-redirect after the user confirms

known_problems.problem: cached results after deploys or content changes
a finding class does not apply to the site
known_problems.workaround: disable it in squirrel.toml or the website's disable_rules and re-audit
